reason: README progress and no-game-code wording need reconciliation with committed src/partial. Further source-specific evidence needed before promoting semantic recovery claim.

title: Next MS Engine — Spectrum Next
reason: Boriel ZX BASIC/Nextlib framework derived conceptually from reduced MK1 for Shovel Adventure and expanded with Next features. Actual player and game-loop source inspected.

title: CUBIX — 6809 SBC operating-system ports
reason: Dave Dunfield CUBIX adapted for Nhyodyne, Duodyne and 6809PC with boot/drivers, applications and toolchain source. Keep whole repository and platform distinctions; no claim that every included application runs on every board.

title: Sargon CP/M emulator experiment
reason: Repository primarily experiments with running generated Sargon Z80 code through a portable Z80 emulator; inspect native CP/M output separately. Keep game-specific emulation out of promoted port listings.

title: Sega CD US BIOS 2.00w — disassembly
reason: Main-68000 BIOS disassembly with constants, structures and decompression routines. README says sub-CPU and Z80 disassemblies are planned, so this is not complete coverage of all processors.

title: The Quill — Sinclair QL database tools
reason: Quill database conversion/listing tools and adventure sources, extending John Elliott's work for QL-specific 32-bit references and command differences. Future PAWS/DAAD goals not treated as implemented.

title: Altered Beast — Mega Drive disassembly
reason: REV02 disassembly with hardware includes, graphics/audio and emulator build workflows. One generated include says Processor 68020; this is a disassembler setting, not evidence the Mega Drive game requires 68020.

title: Donkey King — Color Computer disassembly
reason: Partial annotated listing and exploratory game modifications. Author explicitly acknowledges uncertain 6809/hardware understanding; numeric labels and hypotheses are not established full semantic recovery.

title: BBC portal-engine editor skeleton
reason: Inspected add_vertex command has empty apply and undo bodies. Engine boom is promoted, but the editor needs more implementation evidence before classification as a usable tool.

title: CopperSharp68k — CIL-to-68k compiler
reason: Closed-world ahead-of-time compiler with 68k backend, HUNK/ROM output and Amiga bindings. Supports a bounded .NET profile; planned MorphOS/PPC target and unrestricted .NET compatibility are not promoted.

title: CoCo C development system
reason: Historical compiler, optimizer, linker, libraries and utilities collection. Inspected code-generation source retains modification history. Keep repository collection whole; tool availability and buildability not independently verified.

title: Jurassic Park SNES disassembly
reason: USA1.0 source in SNES ROM Framework with asset extraction and readable SPC engine. Headerless original required; no unsupported regional builds or independent matching result claimed.

title: Yoshi’s Island SNES disassembly
reason: US1.0 disassembly with 65816, Super FX and sound code, credited to Raidenthequick and TheGreekBrit. Upstream calls assembly complete but semantic documentation incomplete; clean-ROM claim not independently tested.

title: Mega Drive Game Genie placeholder
reason: Only README and ROM binary present at reviewed commit; no assembly listing or analysis implementation established.

title: tools7800 development converters
reason: YAML sprites and TMX tiles become cc7800-specific C data, with MARIA layout keywords. Fat-pixel and sprite-height constraints explicit; output is not portable ordinary C for all compilers.

title: zasm Z80-family assembler
reason: 8080/Z80/Z180/Z80N assembler with syntax conversion, tape outputs, optional SDCC and generated-code tests. Decoder/parser bodies reviewed; target-mode differences and external compiler requirements retained.

title: Apple Pascal 1.3 system reconstruction
reason: Pascal/compiler/editor/system sources rebuilt through original tools. Upstream accounts separately for matching file bytes, copied PASCALIO segment, linker slack and disk-image differences; no blanket 100% reconstruction claim.

title: NGPalTool Neo Geo palette editor
reason: Palette conversion/editor with explicit5-bit RGB and dark-bit representation plus palette/export formats. Small source-backed tool, not broad graphics conversion or verified hardware colour matching.

title: ManifeST Atari ST disk cataloguer
reason: Qt/SQLite catalogue with disk-engine integration,hashes and heuristic title/signature detection. Incremental path/mtime/size skipping differs from deep content hashes; early-development speed and accuracy claims not independently tested.

title: FTPMount Amiga handler backport
reason: Work-in-progress backport of AmigaOS4 FTP filesystem fixes to OS3/68k. Source depends on Roadshow SDK, NDK and remaining installation package; no general claim of a finished or securely modernised FTP client.

title: Maniac Mansion EXEPACK unpacker
reason: Kotlin implementation for a specific enhanced EGA MANIAC.EXE hash. Author later identified Microsoft EXEPACK; not a general game reconstruction and output only claimed close to original unpacked executable.

title: jaegonlee/boogaboo_disasm_msx
reason: GitHub cross-fork comparison against tracked mcolom/boogaboo_disasm_msx shows 0 ahead and 0 behind. No unique committed work at reviewed tip; retain tracked upstream rather than add duplicate.

title: Atomic AGD script compiler
reason: Kees van Oss Atom adaptation of Jonathan Cauldwell AGD. C script vocabulary retains historical Z80-style comments, while supplied engine uses concrete 6502 Atom hardware addresses; target CPU determined from implementation rather than stale comments.

title: IDA 6.x 65816 processor module
reason: IDA SDK-derived 65816 processor extension with opcode tables and bank tracking. Targets IDA 6.x and expected SDK 6.9; incompatible new API versions must not be presented as current IDA support. Separate SNES loader dependency retained.

title: Ghidra NES parsing scripts
reason: Small work-in-progress iNES parser and Ghidra loader helpers. Header extraction is real, but hard-coded vector offsets and limited loader code prevent treating it as universal mapper support or complete game decompilation.

title: Lemonade Stand C# source port
reason: Direct adaptation of 1979 Applesoft BASIC with original statements retained in comments and tests. Source-derived port, not binary decompilation; README's planned refactoring does not establish behavior-perfect modern reconstruction. Compared with tracked lars-erik version: this uses direct BASIC-commented Game.cs, while the other uses separate command/domain/calculation classes; shared original subject is not URL identity or duplicated code architecture.

title: Neo Geo Palette Finder
reason: Visual palette-candidate PNG generation from raw ROM/memory bytes, including shifted alignment. Concrete GML bit decoding inspected; not a semantic palette locator. Source comment explicitly credits a ChatGPT-assisted size calculation, not whole-project authorship.

title: Oric Screen Editor
reason: Native text-screen/charset editor with serial attributes and viewport helpers, derived from VDCSE. File picker is limited to SEDORIC3 disks made by TAP2DSK; storage/canvas constraints explicit and advertised editing features not independently runtime-tested.

title: Original QuickDraw source archive
reason: Bill Atkinson's original QuickDraw source mirrored from Computer History Museum material; actual BitBlt and graphics routines inspected. Apple notice permits noncommercial use only, not a general open-source licence; historical source not a current build.

title: TRS-80 terminal and transfer tools
reason: BASIC terminal, Intel HEX helpers and actual assembly terminal code including Model 4 variant. README checklist lags source; do not call assembly absent, but ANSI/keyboard and robust transfer completeness remain unproven.

title: DBW-Render — preserved Amiga ray-tracer Windows port
reason: This is a source-derived native application port and preservation of a legacy ray tracer. The C source retains original 1987 attribution and the IBM-PC port history. No binary-derived decompilation or reverse-engineering methodology is asserted, so the work-kind list is left empty rather than mislabelling a source port.

title: Donkey Kong Junior — Game & Watch conversion for Commodore computers
reason: 6502 assembly conversion of the Game & Watch Donkey Kong Junior game, written with KickAssembler. README identifies C64, VIC-20, C16, C116 and Plus/4 versions. Native game source implements input, enemies, scoring, lives and frame/tick loops. No independently verified build or run is claimed.

title: JagLBA
reason: A substantial source-derived native Atari Jaguar port of Little Big Adventure with documented GPL engine lineage, 68000 execution, Jaguar GPU/DSP rendering work and an explicit work-in-progress boundary.

title: Oric_MiSTer
reason: Maintained Oric-1, Atmos and Pravetz 8D FPGA core with media tooling.

title: RetroIO
reason: Documented Go tooling inspects several 8-bit disk/tape formats, directories, geometry and Spectrum BASIC.

title: TRS-80 Model 102 ROM — documented source reconstruction
reason: Primary repository evidence establishes a distinct, implemented project within the tracker scope at the recorded classification and evidence boundary.

title: bin2fds — FDSStick capture-to-disk-image converter
reason: Narrow Python 2 converter; upstream describes limited success Parses FDS disk blocks and Nintendo-HVC headers from BIN captures, computes CRC diagnostics and emits an FDS header with padded 65,500-byte sides. Handles multiple input sides and rejects an existing output path; substantive recovery implementation rather than a file-extension renamer. Requires legacy Python 2, not Python 3. README says it only sometimes converts captures that other tooling failed to preserve. Code diagnoses CRC mismatches and can skip unexpected data; this is not proof of exact or complete recovery. Test against known-good source data before relying on an output. MIT license covers the tool, not original game disk contents. No input image was decoded during this review.

title: Dork's Dilemma — C16 / Plus4 source restoration
reason: Substantial original-source modules, ca65 conversion and annotated missing-function reconstruction from original binary. Build targets c16 and assembles native 6502; provenance and reconstruction process documented. Author explicitly reports rebuilt binary display broken; assembly success is not playability. Fixed-address calls and routine reconstruction not independently verified. README contains inconsistent older build examples; current build.sh uses c16-final.cfg and suppresses linker status through a pipeline. No clean build or runtime test. Author reports successful assembly and execution with broken display; current status explicitly says no correct game graphics. Compilable/runnable are upstream reports, playable false. build.sh suppresses linker pipeline errors; no independent clean build.

title: re64 collaborative C64 reverse-engineering framework
reason: Active collaborative C64 reverse-engineering framework; source and experiment records available. TypeScript work-queue 6502 disassembler, PRG/D64 loading and structured claims model; MCP/HTTP/WebSocket interfaces share project knowledge. Source implements control-flow warnings, target discovery and memory-layer handling; experiments document agents analyzing programs. Active development; not a game reconstruction itself. README says user header is not authenticated; deploy security not assessed. Game/ROM/reference artifacts have distinct provenance; project MIT label does not license third-party games. README and 11 documented agent-analysis experiment runs establish upstream use of the server/UI/API. npm scripts and Node >=22.5 requirement are reviewed, but compilation/tests were not run. Model/lifter tests are not whole-machine accuracy or game completion.

title: Red Planet — native CPC464 action-adventure
reason: Original/homebrew CPC game built on Mojon Twins MK1/la Churrera. Custom configuration, gameplay, maps, scripts and assets are present. This does not establish a reconstruction of another legacy binary or original authorship of the inherited engine. Released native CPC464 action-adventure source with English and Spanish artifacts; not independently built or played. Windows batch pipeline expects z88dk zcc, cpcrslib and bundled conversion tools. Supplied binaries and upstream release status were not compiled or played here. README says software is GPL v2, but cover artwork by Masterklown is explicitly excluded and requires separate permission. Do not treat the cover as GPL.

title: 64spec — native C64/6502 assembly testing framework
reason: Original MIT KickAssembler framework executes assertions on 6502/C64 state and displays test results. Substantial assembly implements register, flag, memory and comparison assertions; sample specs and framework self-tests are present. Canonical 64bites source is counted once. The c64lib fork is recorded as related build-dependency lineage, not a second independent framework. No test suite or example was assembled or run.

title: CommLib2 — reconstructed C64 RS-232 communications library
reason: Reverse-engineered version of İlker Fıçıcılar’s CommLib2 RS-232 library with actual receive/transmit and setup assembly. Makefile uses KickAssembler through Docker and has c1541 disk-image packaging; README places code at $CA00 and receive buffer at $9000. BASIC users must reserve the receive buffer by reducing top-of-BASIC memory as documented; relocation is an upstream expectation, not verified. No license file was found in the inspected tree; original-library and reconstruction rights remain unclear.

title: CPython 3.12.7 — AmigaOS 4 PowerPC port
reason: PowerPC port of CPython 3.12.7 with native Exec/DOS/Intuition/Graphics bindings, OS-specific patches, newlib/clib4 variants and pure-Python wheel installer. _amigamodule.c contains real Python-to-Amiga native bindings; build.sh specifies powerpc-unknown-amigaos and -mcpu=750. Latest SETUP.md supersedes stale README SSL details: both variants provide HTTPS paths, while clib4 cannot support live-socket TLS wrappers such as requests/httpx. AmigaOS 4.1 Final Edition+; QEMU Sam460ex is upstream tested, real hardware explicitly untested. PPC 750 code generation is not a minimum RAM claim. clib4 needs PYTHONUTF8=1 and clib4.library; both variants disable dynamic C-extension loading. Standard subprocess/pip workflows have OS-specific limitations. README claims MIT for glue and PSF for CPython, but no root LICENSE appears in inspected tree; verify license packaging before redistribution. Build/runtime test counts remain upstream-only.

title: gtlayout.library — preserved Amiga GadTools layout toolkit
reason: LTP_LayoutGadgets.c contains the substantial native gadget layout implementation and optional BOOPSI class loading. SAS/C smakefile compiles the source suite and generates documentation/header material; current CPU setting is ANY, with old 68020 option commented out. README’s future AROS/MorphOS porting intent is not an implemented runtime claim. SAS/C 6.58, NDK 3.2R4, ctags, LibDescConverter and Autodoc are documented dependencies. The source is marked freely distributable; that is not automatically equivalent to a modern permissive license.

title: Magic-Desk-CRT — native C64 cartridge bootstrap and loader
reason: Native KickAssembler bootstrap and loader implement CBM80 startup, relocation and banked Magic Desk cartridge data copying. Loader code switches banks via $DE00 and copies from consecutive 8 KiB banks; author states it was written for Tony: Montezuma’s Gold. Requires correct C64 memory mapping and cartridge visibility. This is a developer library, not a new emulator or a recovered commercial ROM. MIT code license does not automatically establish rights in all bundled film/comic-inspired slideshow images.

title: nettle
reason: Native RISC OS telnet/terminal application source, historically relevant but this repository does not demonstrate recovered historic binary analysis or a specific reverse-engineering tool.

title: alfishe/amiga-bootcamp
reason: Amiga development and internals reference, rather than an implemented retro software or analysis tool.

title: muckypaws/AmstradCPC
reason: Mixed archive of period CPC sources, tools and commercial work; components need individual attribution and scope before promotion.

title: Music-player disassemblies — C64 and Atari 8-bit
reason: Concrete labelled disassembly and sequencer/pattern analysis of C64 International Karate SID and multiple Atari POKEY players, accompanied by Frida projects and source music files. This is subsystem research rather than full-game reconstruction and is kept as one coherent archive.

title: C64 crack-intro disassemblies — Tomaszndt
reason: Five source listings contain concrete C64 intro disassembly with origin links, labels and analysis of raster interrupts, scrolling, system calls and music. Lack of a README/build script does not negate the existing research; catalogue at whole-repository scope.

title: Hägar the Horrible — C64 original-source preservation
reason: Archive preserves programmer-supplied original game sources and disk artifacts and makes the tokenized Turbo Assembler source readable through documented extraction. This is source preservation under the broadened scope, not binary-derived reconstruction or a new disassembly.

title: Return Home — Amstrad CPC Z80 space shooter
reason: Substantial original Z80 game source, RASM build pipeline and ready-to-run CPC disk image demonstrate concrete native homebrew. The custom Z80 emulator/profiler is supporting testing infrastructure; the promoted output is a native CPC game.

title: sidneycadot/Atari8bit_OSB-NTSC-ROM
reason: This is a substantive OCR/proofreading source-restoration and verified ca65 ROM-reconstruction workflow, not an ordinary original-source mirror.
